title: platform work items v1
description: The common work-item format. A repo's file platform/work-items.json is {"schema": "platform-work-items-v1", "items": [ ... ]}. Same field names as the platform's own backlog so one reader works everywhere.

properties.id: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 3 to 60 characters, unique in the file
properties.title: one sentence, at most 200 characters
properties.priority: integer 0 to 100; higher is more urgent
properties.acceptance: how anyone can check it is done; at least 10 characters
properties.depends_on: list of item ids that must be done first
properties.waits_for: optional: what the item waits for, a string `card:<id>`, `owner:<what>`, `item:<id>`, `time:<date>` or `session:<name>` followed by what it waits for. The hub shows and counts it; a `card:` wait on an unanswered card must never stop dev work, so split the dev part off or list the item in inventory/foyer-allowed.json card_blocks.
properties.next_step: one or two sentences, at most 220 characters; required while the item is open and waiting
properties.evidence: list of strings: PR numbers, files, receipts
properties.kind: free label such as fix, enable, measure
properties.ask: optional; when the item needs the owner (owner tito or waiting_on owner): {question, recommended, due (YYYY-MM-DD), default (what the agent assumes after due; null = needs his call), link (http(s) URL or null), steps (optional list of plain step-by-step instructions, at most 12, shown under the row)}. Rendered per product on the hub's owner board.
properties.allowed_paths: optional list of globs: the only paths a worker may change for this item (worker rule 4; the builder job rejects a diff outside them)
properties.files_to_read: optional list of repo paths a builder should read first (at most 30)
properties.tests_to_run: optional list of commands that must pass before the pull request (each a string, run from the repo root)
properties.role: optional: the worker kind, set by a lead or the planner (shared: builder, investigator, researcher, reviewer, repairer, planner; or one from this repo's platform/roles.json). Without it Python resolves it from `kind` through kit/work-types.json (python3 platform/kit/roles.py resolve ITEM_JSON); a kind that does not say what the hand-back is goes to the planner to be labelled. The model never picks its own role.

tested_live.description: The change ran on the real machine: when, and the receipt or observation that proves it. Set on a done item.

owner_accepted.description: The owner saw the result and accepted it: when, and what he said (short quote). Set on a done item.
